quote: In this work, we propose a novel approach to tackle the extended summary generation for scientific documents.

... we test the proposed approach on two publicly available large-scale extended summarization datasets, namely arXiv-Long and PubMed-Long ... Our model is built upon the fine‑tuned contextualized language models for text summarization.

quote: Overall, our model achieves about 1.4%, 2.4%, 3.5% (arXiv-Long), and 1.0%, 2.5%, 1.3% (PubMed-Long) improvements across ROUGE score variants; and 2.2% (arXiv-Long), 1.4% (PubMed-Long) improvements over F1, compared to the neural baselines.
... we report ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L and average ROUGE(F1) scores ...
Our choice of ROUGE-2 and ROUGE-L is based on the fact that these express higher similarity with human judgments.

For the sake of evaluation, two annotators were asked to manually evaluate two sets of 40 papers' groundtruth abstracts (40 for arXiv-Long, and 40 for PubMed-Long) with their generated extended summaries (baselines' and ours) to gain insights into qualities of each model.
guideline: Annotators were asked to specify if the first system-generated summary wins/loses or ties with the second system-generated summary in terms of qualitative metrics.
Annotators compared system‑generated summaries pairwise and marked which summary was better, tied, or worse on the dimensions of cohesion and completeness.

Annotators were asked to specify if the first system-generated summary wins/loses or ties with the second system-generated summary in terms of qualitative metrics: (1) Cohesion: whether the ordering of sentences in summary is cohesive, namely sentences entail each other. (2) Completeness: whether the summary covers all salient information provided in the ground-truth summary.
